1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Off-box backup replication.
3	#
4	# Copies the DB dumps, the host-configuration archives and (optionally) the
5	# whole-system VM archives to an OFFSITE target, so a chassis or disk loss does
6	# not take the backups with it.
7	#
8	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
9	# WHY THIS NOW FAILS INSTEAD OF EXITING 0
10	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
11	# This script used to `exit 0` when no target was configured, with a comment
12	# reading "not an error: intentionally inert until configured". The consequence,
13	# observed on this host: nxeon-backup-offsite.service ran at 04:20 on 2026-07-24,
14	# -07-25 and -07-26 and recorded `Result=success` every time, having copied
15	# nothing anywhere. systemd showed a green unit, the OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook
16	# never fired because nothing failed, and the admin portal had no page that would
17	# have said otherwise. For three days the platform reported working off-site
18	# backups while every byte it owned lived on one pool in one chassis.
19	#
20	# An inert backup that reports OK is worse than no backup at all: no backup at
21	# least leaves the operator's belief accurate. So an unconfigured target is now a
22	# hard failure — non-zero exit, systemd unit red, admin notification via
23	# nxeon-alert@ — and it stays red until someone actually configures a target or
24	# explicitly, deliberately acknowledges the risk.
25	#
26	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27	# WHAT THE OWNER MUST SET
28	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	# Edit /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env and set exactly ONE of:
30	#
31	#   OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups"
32	#       An rclone remote (Backblaze B2, S3, OVH/Hetzner object storage, …).
33	#       Requires: apt install rclone && rclone config — configure the remote as
34	#       ROOT, because this unit runs as root and reads root's
35	#       ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf.
36	#
37	#   OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="user@host:/backups/nxeon"
38	#       rsync over SSH (rsync.net, a second box, a NAS). Requires key-based auth
39	#       for root with no passphrase prompt: ssh-keygen, ssh-copy-id, then verify
40	#       `ssh -o BatchMode=yes user@host true` succeeds as root.
41	#
42	#   OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE="/nxeon-backups"
43	#       A Mega (mega.io / mega.nz) account, via the `megatools` CLI (`megacopy`,
44	#       `megals`, `megamkdir`, `megarm`) — NOT the official `megacmd` suite, which
45	#       is not in this host's apt mirror and would require adding Mega's own repo
46	#       (unverified for Debian trixie at the time this was written; flagged for
47	#       a human to evaluate if `megatools` proves insufficient). `megatools` IS
48	#       directly installable from the existing configured mirror:
49	#         apt install megatools
50	#       Also requires, in THIS SAME env file:
51	#         MEGA_EMAIL="you@example.com"
52	#         MEGA_PASSWORD="..."
53	#       Credentials are never passed on the command line (visible to any local
54	#       user via /proc/<pid>/cmdline) — this script writes them to a 0600
55	#       temp `--config` file for megatools and shreds it when the run ends, win
56	#       or lose (see the `MEGA_CFG` trap below).
57	#       Optional: OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN=1 runs `megacopy -n` (megatools' real
58	#       dry-run flag — "don't perform any actual changes, just print what would
59	#       be done") instead of a live upload. Use this for the first test after
60	#       setting credentials, BEFORE trusting it with real backup data.
61	#       megacopy itself never overwrites or deletes remote files (upload-only,
62	#       by megatools' own design) — see lib/offsite-retention.ts and the prune
63	#       step in `sync_one` below for how this script keeps Mega storage from
64	#       growing forever anyway.
65	#
66	# Optional:
67	#   OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1        also replicate the whole-system VM archives.
68	#                                Large (tens of GB/day) but this is the only copy
69	#                                that survives losing the chassis. Strongly
70	#                                recommended once bandwidth allows.
71	#   OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1      acknowledge "no off-site copy exists" and exit 0.
72	#                                ONLY for a deliberately single-chassis
73	#                                deployment. This is the switch that turns the
74	#                                alarm off; there is no other.
75	#
76	# SECURITY: the host-configuration archives contain /etc/pve/priv (cluster and CA
77	# private keys) and /etc/nxeon (Proxmox API token, Cloudflare token, mail
78	# credentials). Whatever target you choose therefore holds the keys to this
79	# platform. Use an rclone `crypt` remote, a target you control with at-rest
80	# encryption, or Mega's own account-level encryption — never a shared or public
81	# bucket/account.
82	#
83	# Exits non-zero on any real failure so the systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins.
84	set -uo pipefail
85	
86	ENV_FILE="/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env"
87	SRC_DB="/tank/backup/db"
88	SRC_PLATFORM="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
89	STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
90	STATUS="${STATUS_DIR}/offsite.json"
91	# The Nxeon app checkout — where lib/offsite-retention.ts and
92	# scripts/mega-prune-plan.ts live, invoked via its own node_modules/tsx.
93	NXEON_APP_DIR="${NXEON_APP_DIR:-/opt/nxeon}"
94	# Running total of files pruned off Mega this run, surfaced in the status JSON.
95	MEGA_PRUNED_TOTAL=0
96	# Path to the ephemeral megatools config file, set only when KIND=mega actually
97	# runs. Declared here so the EXIT trap below can always reference it safely.
98	MEGA_CFG=""
99	
100	log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }
101	
102	mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true
103	
104	# Credentials never linger on disk longer than this run, success or failure.
105	cleanup_mega_cfg() { [ -n "${MEGA_CFG}" ] && [ -f "${MEGA_CFG}" ] && shred -u "${MEGA_CFG}" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "${MEGA_CFG}" 2>/dev/null || true; }
106	trap cleanup_mega_cfg EXIT
107	
108	# The status file is what /admin/backups reads. The panel runs as the unprivileged
109	# `nxeon` user and cannot read /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env (0600 root), so this
110	# is the only channel by which the portal can tell the owner the truth about
111	# off-site state — and it deliberately records the target KIND, never its value,
112	# so a bucket name or SSH host never leaks into a web page.
113	write_status() {
114	    local ok="$1" configured="$2" kind="$3" detail="$4"
115	    local last_success="null"
116	    # Preserve the previous successful-sync timestamp across a failing run, so the
117	    # panel can say "configured, but last succeeded 6 days ago" rather than losing
118	    # the only evidence that it ever worked.
119	    if [ "${ok}" = "true" ]; then
120	        last_success="\"$(date -Is)\""
121	    elif [ -f "${STATUS}" ]; then
122	        local prev
123	        prev="$(sed -n 's/.*"lastSuccessAt":\("[^"]*"\|null\).*/\1/p' "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
124	        [ -n "${prev}" ] && last_success="${prev}"
125	    fi
126	    printf '{"ok":%s,"configured":%s,"kind":"%s","at":"%s","lastSuccessAt":%s,"detail":"%s","prunedRemote":%s}\n' \
127	        "${ok}" "${configured}" "${kind}" "$(date -Is)" "${last_success}" "${detail}" "${MEGA_PRUNED_TOTAL}" > "${STATUS}"
128	    chmod 644 "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null || true
129	}
130	
131	[ -f "${ENV_FILE}" ] && . "${ENV_FILE}"
132	
133	OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE:-}"
134	OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET:-}"
135	OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE="${OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE:-}"
136	MEGA_EMAIL="${MEGA_EMAIL:-}"
137	MEGA_PASSWORD="${MEGA_PASSWORD:-}"
138	OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN="${OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN:-0}"
139	OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS="${OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS:-0}"
140	OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET="${OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET:-0}"
141	
142	# How many of the three target kinds are actually set — used for both the
143	# "none configured" and "more than one configured" checks below.
144	TARGETS_SET=0
145	[ -n "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}" ] && TARGETS_SET=$((TARGETS_SET + 1))
146	[ -n "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}" ] && TARGETS_SET=$((TARGETS_SET + 1))
147	[ -n "${OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE}" ] && TARGETS_SET=$((TARGETS_SET + 1))
148	
149	if [ "${TARGETS_SET}" -eq 0 ]; then
150	    if [ "${OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET}" = "1" ]; then
151	        log "off-site replication DISABLED and acknowledged (OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1)"
152	        log "every backup this platform holds lives only on this chassis — accepted by the operator"
153	        write_status true false acknowledged "disabled and acknowledged by the operator"
154	        exit 0
155	    fi
156	    log "=============================================================="
157	    log "FAIL: OFF-SITE BACKUPS ARE NOT CONFIGURED"
158	    log "Every backup this platform holds — the customer database, the VM"
159	    log "archives, the /etc/pve definitions — exists on exactly ONE pool in"
160	    log "ONE chassis. Losing this box loses all of it, and that means losing"
161	    log "every customer's data with no recovery path."
162	    log ""
163	    log "Set exactly ONE of these in ${ENV_FILE}:"
164	    log "  OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE=\"b2:nxeon-backups\"        (apt install rclone; rclone config as root)"
165	    log "  OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET=\"user@host:/backups/nxeon\"  (root key-based SSH, BatchMode must work)"
166	    log "  OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE=\"/nxeon-backups\"             (apt install megatools; set MEGA_EMAIL/MEGA_PASSWORD too)"
167	    log ""
168	    log "Optional: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 to replicate the VM archives too."
169	    log "If this host is deliberately single-chassis, set OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1"
170	    log "to acknowledge the risk and silence this failure. Do not silence it any"
171	    log "other way: this unit reporting success while copying nothing is exactly"
172	    log "the state it spent 2026-07-24..26 in."
173	    log "=============================================================="
174	    write_status false false none "no OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE, OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET or OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE set"
175	    exit 1
176	fi
177	
178	if [ "${TARGETS_SET}" -gt 1 ]; then
179	    log "FAIL: more than one of OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE / OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET / OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE is set — pick exactly one"
180	    write_status false true ambiguous "more than one offsite target is set"
181	    exit 1
182	fi
183	
184	if [ -n "${OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE}" ] && { [ -z "${MEGA_EMAIL}" ] || [ -z "${MEGA_PASSWORD}" ]; }; then
185	    log "FAIL: OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE is set but MEGA_EMAIL and/or MEGA_PASSWORD is missing from ${ENV_FILE}"
186	    write_status false true mega "OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE set without MEGA_EMAIL/MEGA_PASSWORD"
187	    exit 1
188	fi
189	
190	KIND="rsync"
191	[ -n "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}" ] && KIND="rclone"
192	[ -n "${OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE}" ] && KIND="mega"
193	
194	if [ "${KIND}" = "mega" ]; then
195	    command -v megacopy >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: megatools not installed (apt install megatools)"; write_status false true mega "megatools not installed"; exit 1; }
196	    MEGA_CFG="$(mktemp /tmp/nxeon-offsite-mega.XXXXXX)" || { log "FAIL: mktemp for mega config"; exit 1; }
197	    chmod 600 "${MEGA_CFG}"
198	    # See megarc(5): [Login] section, Username/Password keys. Written fresh each
199	    # run and shredded on exit (trap set above) — never left on disk, never
200	    # passed as a CLI argument (which /proc/<pid>/cmdline would leak to any
201	    # local user).
202	    {
203	        printf '[Login]\n'
204	        printf 'Username = %s\n' "${MEGA_EMAIL}"
205	        printf 'Password = %s\n' "${MEGA_PASSWORD}"
206	    } > "${MEGA_CFG}"
207	fi
208	
209	if [ ! -d "${SRC_DB}" ]; then
210	    log "FAIL: ${SRC_DB} missing — there is nothing to replicate, which is itself the problem"
211	    write_status false true "${KIND}" "source ${SRC_DB} missing"
212	    exit 1
213	fi
214	
215	# sync_one replicates one directory and then VERIFIES the target actually holds
216	# files. A transport that exits 0 without transferring anything (wrong remote
217	# path, silently empty source, an rclone remote pointing at a deleted bucket) is
218	# the same class of lie this script was rewritten to stop telling.
219	sync_one() {
220	    local src="$1" label="$2" rc=0
221	    local n_src
222	    n_src=$(find "${src}" -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name '*.partial' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
223	    if [ "${n_src}" -eq 0 ]; then
224	        log "FAIL: ${label}: source ${src} holds no files — refusing to report a successful sync"
225	        return 1
226	    fi
227	
228	    if [ "${KIND}" = "mega" ]; then
229	        local remote_dir="${OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE%/}/${label}"
230	        local dryflag=()
231	        if [ "${OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN}" = "1" ]; then
232	            dryflag=(-n)
233	            log "megacopy ${label} [DRY RUN]: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> mega:${remote_dir}"
234	        else
235	            log "megacopy ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> mega:${remote_dir}"
236	        fi
237	        # Best-effort: the remote dir may already exist, or megacopy may create
238	        # it itself — either way this must never be treated as the failure.
239	        megamkdir --config "${MEGA_CFG}" "${remote_dir}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
240	        megacopy --config "${MEGA_CFG}" --local "${src}" --remote "${remote_dir}" \
241	            --no-progress "${dryflag[@]}" || rc=$?
242	        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} megacopy exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
243	
244	        if [ "${OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN}" = "1" ]; then
245	            log "OK ${label} dry-run completed — no changes made (OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN=1)"
246	            return 0
247	        fi
248	
249	        # Post-sync assertion: Mega must now list files, same discipline as the
250	        # rclone/rsync paths above.
251	        local n_dst
252	        n_dst=$(megals --config "${MEGA_CFG}" "${remote_dir}" 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)
253	        n_dst="${n_dst:-0}"
254	        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
255	            log "FAIL: ${label}: mega remote lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
256	            return 1
257	        fi
258	        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on Mega)"
259	
260	        # Mirror-prune: megacopy is documented to never overwrite or delete
261	        # remote files, so anything LOCAL retention rotated out (backup-db.sh /
262	        # backup-vms.sh / backup-pve-config.sh keep-last policies) would
263	        # otherwise pile up on Mega forever. See lib/offsite-retention.ts for
264	        # the pure decision logic behind this — this just feeds it names.
265	        local to_delete pruned=0
266	        to_delete=$(megals --config "${MEGA_CFG}" "${remote_dir}" 2>/dev/null | \
267	            (cd "${NXEON_APP_DIR}" && npx --no-install tsx scripts/mega-prune-plan.ts "${src}") 2>/dev/null || true)
268	        if [ -n "${to_delete}" ]; then
269	            while IFS= read -r name; do
270	                [ -z "${name}" ] && continue
271	                if megarm --config "${MEGA_CFG}" "${remote_dir}/${name}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
272	                    pruned=$((pruned + 1))
273	                else
274	                    log "WARN: failed to prune ${remote_dir}/${name} from Mega (will retry next run)"
275	                fi
276	            done <<< "${to_delete}"
277	            log "pruned ${pruned} file(s) from mega:${remote_dir} no longer present locally"
278	        fi
279	        MEGA_PRUNED_TOTAL=$((MEGA_PRUNED_TOTAL + pruned))
280	    elif [ "${KIND}" = "rclone" ]; then
281	        command -v rclone >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rclone not installed (apt install rclone)"; return 1; }
282	        log "rclone sync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <remote>/${label}"
283	        rclone sync "${src}" "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" \
284	            --transfers 4 --retries 3 --exclude '*.partial' || rc=$?
285	        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rclone exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
286	        # Post-sync assertion: the remote must now list files.
287	        local n_dst
288	        n_dst=$(rclone lsf "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
289	        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
290	            log "FAIL: ${label}: remote lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
291	            return 1
292	        fi
293	        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the remote)"
294	    else
295	        command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rsync not installed"; return 1; }
296	        log "rsync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <target>/${label}"
297	        rsync -az --delete --exclude '*.partial' \
298	            -e "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=20" \
299	            "${src}/" "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}/${label}/" || rc=$?
300	        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rsync exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
301	        # Post-sync assertion: count files on the far side over the same transport.
302	        local host="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET%%:*}" path="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET#*:}" n_dst
303	        n_dst=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 "${host}" \
304	            "find '${path}/${label}' -maxdepth 1 -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
305	        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
306	            log "FAIL: ${label}: target lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
307	            return 1
308	        fi
309	        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the target)"
310	    fi
311	}
312	
313	fail=0
314	synced=""
315	
316	if sync_one "${SRC_DB}" "db"; then synced="${synced}db "; else fail=1; fi
317	
318	# The host-configuration archives are ~50 KB and are the difference between
319	# "restore the VMs" and "rebuild every VM definition from memory". They are
320	# replicated unconditionally: there is no bandwidth argument against 50 KB.
321	# Staged into a temp dir so the VM archives in the same directory are not dragged
322	# along when OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS is off.
323	if [ -d "${SRC_PLATFORM}" ] && compgen -G "${SRC_PLATFORM}/host-config-*.tar.gz" >/dev/null; then
324	    if tmpdir="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-offsite-config.XXXXXX)"; then
325	        cp -p "${SRC_PLATFORM}"/host-config-*.tar.gz "${tmpdir}/" 2>/dev/null
326	        if sync_one "${tmpdir}" "host-config"; then synced="${synced}host-config "; else fail=1; fi
327	        rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
328	    else
329	        log "FAIL: could not stage host-config archives for replication"
330	        fail=1
331	    fi
332	else
333	    log "FAIL: no host-config-*.tar.gz in ${SRC_PLATFORM} — /etc/pve is not being captured."
334	    log "      Run scripts/backup-pve-config.sh (or the nxeon-backup-vms unit, which calls it)."
335	    fail=1
336	fi
337	
338	if [ "${OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS}" = "1" ]; then
339	    if [ -d "${SRC_PLATFORM}" ]; then
340	        if sync_one "${SRC_PLATFORM}" "vms"; then synced="${synced}vms "; else fail=1; fi
341	    else
342	        log "FAIL: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 but ${SRC_PLATFORM} does not exist"
343	        fail=1
344	    fi
345	else
346	    log "note: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS is not set — VM archives are NOT replicated off-site."
347	    log "      A chassis loss would still cost every VM image. Set OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 when bandwidth allows."
348	fi
349	
350	if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
351	    write_status false true "${KIND}" "one or more replication targets failed"
352	    log "off-site replication FAILED"
353	    exit 1
354	fi
355	
356	write_status true true "${KIND}" "replicated: ${synced% }"
357	log "off-site replication complete (${synced% })"

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Nxeon — whole-system backup (host config + every guest), run DAILY, keep 3.
3	#
4	# Step 1: scripts/backup-pve-config.sh  — /etc/pve and friends (see that file).
5	# Step 2: vzdump of every QEMU guest with VMID in [100, 9000), plus the OS
6	#         templates when NXEON_VM_BACKUP_INCLUDE_TEMPLATES=1 (the default).
7	#
8	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
9	# WHERE THESE ARCHIVES GO, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE `backup` STORAGE
10	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
11	# This script used to run `vzdump --storage backup`, which writes into
12	# /tank/backup/dump — the same Proxmox storage a customer's own on-demand backups
13	# land in. lib/proxmox.ts `pruneBackups` then selected deletion victims with
14	# nothing but `b.vmid === vmid`, so a customer clicking "Create backup" pruned
15	# *every* archive for their VMID down to CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP (2) — including the
16	# platform's host-level disaster-recovery copy of that same VM. On 2026-07-26 the
17	# 04:31 run left vmid 102 holding the customer's manual archive plus a 10 GB
18	# platform archive; one more customer click would have destroyed the platform's
19	# only copy. Repeat across the fleet and the entire bare-metal recovery set is
20	# gone, deleted by customers, with no error anywhere.
21	#
22	# So platform archives now go to NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR (/tank/backup/platform)
23	# via `vzdump --dumpdir`. That directory is NOT the `dump/` subdirectory of any
24	# configured PVE storage, and Proxmox only indexes `<storage-path>/dump`. The
25	# archives therefore have no `volid`: they cannot appear in the
26	# /storage/backup/content listing that customer retention iterates, and no volid
27	# string exists that `DELETE /storage/backup/content/<volid>` could resolve to
28	# them. Customer retention cannot reach them because it cannot name them.
29	#
30	# vzdump's own `--prune-backups` still works in dumpdir mode (PVE::VZDump
31	# get_backup_file_list + prune_mark_backup_group), scoped to files matching
32	# `vzdump-<type>-<vmid>-*` inside that one directory — so platform retention only
33	# ever prunes platform archives.
34	#
35	# FALLBACK MODE: setting NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE=<sid> restores the old
36	# shared-storage behaviour for operators who want these visible in the Proxmox UI.
37	# In that mode every archive is stamped with `--notes-template` carrying the
38	# platform marker and its volid is appended to PROTECTED-VOLIDS, both of which
39	# lib/proxmox.ts honours — so the invariant holds there too, just by convention
40	# rather than by construction. Dumpdir mode is the default for that reason.
41	#
42	# Idempotent / re-runnable. Never deletes anything but its own aged-out archives.
43	set -uo pipefail
44	
45	PLATFORM_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
46	STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
47	REGISTRY="${PLATFORM_DIR}/PROTECTED-VOLIDS"
48	# Owner's stated policy: "back up the entire system once every day, store the
49	# latest 3." Daily cadence lives in nxeon-backup-vms.timer; the 3 lives here.
50	KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"
51	# Empty = dumpdir mode (recommended, see above). Non-empty = shared PVE storage.
52	STORAGE="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE:-}"
53	INCLUDE_TEMPLATES="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_INCLUDE_TEMPLATES:-1}"
54	MARKER="NXEON-PLATFORM-BACKUP"
55	
56	log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }
57	
58	rc=0
59	status_dir_ready=0
60	mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && status_dir_ready=1
61	
62	write_status() {
63	    [ "${status_dir_ready}" = "1" ] || return 0
64	    printf '{"ok":%s,"at":"%s","mode":"%s","dest":"%s","keepLast":%s,"vmids":"%s","error":%s}\n' \
65	        "$1" "$(date -Is)" "$([ -n "${STORAGE}" ] && echo storage || echo dumpdir)" \
66	        "$([ -n "${STORAGE}" ] && echo "${STORAGE}" || echo "${PLATFORM_DIR}")" \
67	        "${KEEP_LAST}" "${2:-}" "$3" > "${STATUS_DIR}/vm-backup.json"
68	    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/vm-backup.json" 2>/dev/null || true
69	}
70	
71	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
72	# Step 1 — host configuration. Cheapest and most irreplaceable, so it goes first
73	# and a failure here does NOT skip the guest dumps (but does fail the unit, so the
74	# OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook still notifies the admins).
75	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
76	CONFIG_SCRIPT="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/backup-pve-config.sh"
77	if [ "${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
78	    log "DRY RUN — would run ${CONFIG_SCRIPT} (host configuration backup)"
79	elif [ -x "${CONFIG_SCRIPT}" ]; then
80	    log "step 1/2 — host configuration (/etc/pve, /etc/nxeon, units)"
81	    if ! "${CONFIG_SCRIPT}"; then
82	        log "ERROR host configuration backup failed — continuing with guest dumps"
83	        rc=1
84	    fi
85	else
86	    log "ERROR ${CONFIG_SCRIPT} missing or not executable — /etc/pve is NOT being backed up"
87	    rc=1
88	fi
89	
90	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	# Step 2 — guests.
92	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
93	# Customer + platform guests: 100 <= VMID < 9000.
94	mapfile -t VMIDS < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}' | sort -n)
95	# OS templates (9000+). They are reproducible via scripts/build-templates.sh, but
96	# reproducing them takes hours of cloud-image downloads and customisation, and a
97	# provision cannot run without them — so a daily copy is worth its (highly sparse)
98	# few GB. Set NXEON_VM_BACKUP_INCLUDE_TEMPLATES=0 to skip.
99	if [ "${INCLUDE_TEMPLATES}" = "1" ]; then
100	    mapfile -t TPLIDS < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=9000 {print $1}' | sort -n)
101	    VMIDS+=("${TPLIDS[@]}")
102	fi
103	# Drop any empty element, defensively.
104	#
105	# These expansions used to be written `"${ARR[@]:-}"`. On an EMPTY array that does
106	# not expand to nothing — `:-` substitutes its (empty) default, yielding exactly
107	# ONE empty-string element. So when `qm list` returned no guests (pve-cluster down,
108	# qm absent, a parse change) the array ended up with length 1, the
109	# `[ "${#VMIDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]` guard below could never fire, and the script ran
110	# `vzdump "" --dumpdir ...` — passing an empty vmid to a tool whose job is to act
111	# on every guest you name. The "host configuration backup only" path was
112	# unreachable code.
113	#
114	# bash 5.2 (this host) expands "${ARR[@]}" on an empty array to nothing under
115	# `set -u`, which is what was intended; the `:-` was working around a bash < 4.4
116	# behaviour that does not apply here and silently changed the meaning.
117	CLEAN=()
118	for v in "${VMIDS[@]}"; do [ -n "${v}" ] && CLEAN+=("${v}"); done
119	VMIDS=("${CLEAN[@]}")
120	
121	if [ "${#VMIDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
122	    log "no eligible guests found; host configuration backup only"
123	    write_status "$([ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] && echo true || echo false)" "" 'null'
124	    exit "${rc}"
125	fi
126	
127	log "eligible guests: ${VMIDS[*]}"
128	
129	# Build the vzdump argument list. --storage and --dumpdir are mutually exclusive
130	# (PVE::VZDump dies if both are given), and notes-template/protected are silently
131	# dropped by vzdump in dumpdir mode, so the two modes take different arguments.
132	VZ_ARGS=(--compress zstd --mode snapshot --prune-backups "keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}")
133	if [ -n "${STORAGE}" ]; then
134	    VZ_ARGS+=(--storage "${STORAGE}" --notes-template "${MARKER} {{guestname}} {{node}}")
135	    DEST_DESC="PVE storage '${STORAGE}' (shared with customer backups — marker mode)"
136	else
137	    if ! mkdir -p "${PLATFORM_DIR}"; then
138	        log "ERROR cannot create ${PLATFORM_DIR}"
139	        write_status false "${VMIDS[*]}" '"cannot create platform dir"'
140	        exit 1
141	    fi
142	    chmod 755 "${PLATFORM_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true
143	    VZ_ARGS+=(--dumpdir "${PLATFORM_DIR}")
144	    DEST_DESC="${PLATFORM_DIR} (outside every PVE storage — unreachable by customer retention)"
145	fi
146	
147	if [ "${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
148	    log "DRY RUN — would run: vzdump ${VMIDS[*]} ${VZ_ARGS[*]}"
149	    log "DRY RUN — destination: ${DEST_DESC}"
150	    exit "${rc}"
151	fi
152	
153	log "step 2/2 — vzdump ${#VMIDS[@]} guest(s) -> ${DEST_DESC}, zstd/snapshot, keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"
154	if ! vzdump "${VMIDS[@]}" "${VZ_ARGS[@]}"; then
155	    log "ERROR vzdump reported a failure"
156	    rc=1
157	fi
158	
159	# In shared-storage mode the archives ARE addressable by volid, so record them in
160	# the protection registry lib/proxmox.ts fails closed against. Rebuilt from the
161	# live storage listing each run, so pruned archives drop out and nothing grows
162	# without bound. Dumpdir mode needs no registry — there are no volids to protect.
163	if [ -n "${STORAGE}" ]; then
164	    if tmp="$(mktemp "${REGISTRY}.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"; then
165	        {
166	            echo "# Nxeon platform archives on shared storage '${STORAGE}' — customer retention must NEVER delete these."
167	            echo "# Generated by scripts/backup-vms.sh at $(date -Is). Read by lib/proxmox.ts."
168	            # Preserve any hand-seeded entries from a previous file (e.g. archives
169	            # written before the dumpdir split) so this rebuild never un-protects.
170	            [ -f "${REGISTRY}" ] && grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:backup/' "${REGISTRY}" 2>/dev/null
171	            pvesm list "${STORAGE}" --content backup 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 {print $1}'
172	        } | grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:backup/|^#' | awk '!seen[$0]++' > "${tmp}"
173	        chmod 644 "${tmp}" && mv "${tmp}" "${REGISTRY}"
174	        log "protection registry rebuilt: $(grep -cE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:backup/' "${REGISTRY}") volid(s)"
175	    else
176	        log "ERROR could not write ${REGISTRY} — platform archives on shared storage are UNPROTECTED"
177	        rc=1
178	    fi
179	fi
180	
181	# Assert something was actually produced. A "successful" run that wrote no archive
182	# is the exact class of silent failure this platform has already shipped once.
183	if [ -z "${STORAGE}" ]; then
184	    produced=$(find "${PLATFORM_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'vzdump-*' -newermt '-6 hours' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
185	    if [ "${produced}" -eq 0 ]; then
186	        log "ERROR no vzdump archive appeared in ${PLATFORM_DIR} in the last 6h"
187	        rc=1
188	    else
189	        log "${produced} archive file(s) written in the last 6h"
190	    fi
191	fi
192	
193	write_status "$([ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] && echo true || echo false)" "${VMIDS[*]}" \
194	    "$([ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] && echo null || echo '"see journalctl -u nxeon-backup-vms"')"
195	
196	log "done (exit ${rc})"
197	exit "${rc}"
198

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Nxeon — host configuration backup (the bare-metal rebuild set).
3	#
4	# WHY THIS EXISTS: nothing on this box backed up /etc/pve. The VM *disks* were
5	# being dumped by vzdump, but /etc/pve/qemu-server/<vmid>.conf — the file that
6	# says how much RAM a guest has, which bridge and MAC its NIC uses, which disks
7	# it owns and in what order, plus /etc/pve/storage.cfg, /etc/pve/user.cfg and the
8	# firewall rules — existed in exactly one place: this chassis. After a total host
9	# loss you would have had a directory full of vzdump archives and no VM
10	# definitions to restore them into, no storage named `vmdata` for them to land
11	# on, and no record of the network layout. `qmrestore` reads the config out of
12	# the archive for the guest itself, but the *host* side (storage.cfg, bridges,
13	# users, ACLs, the Nxeon systemd units) would have had to be reconstructed from
14	# memory. This script is small, fast (~16 KB of config) and runs before the
15	# multi-gigabyte guest dumps so the cheapest, most irreplaceable data is
16	# captured first.
17	#
18	# Also snapshots the *interpretation* of that config (pvesm status, pveversion,
19	# zpool status, ip addr) as plain text, because a rebuild is done by a human
20	# reading it, not only by a machine restoring it.
21	#
22	# Idempotent / re-runnable. Deletes nothing except its own aged-out archives.
23	set -uo pipefail
24	
25	DEST_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
26	STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
27	KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_CONFIG_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"
28	TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
29	DEST="${DEST_DIR}/host-config-${TS}.tar.gz"
30	
31	log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }
32	
33	mkdir -p "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" || { log "FAIL: cannot create ${DEST_DIR}"; exit 1; }
34	chmod 755 "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true
35	
36	if [ ! -d /etc/pve ]; then
37	    log "FAIL: /etc/pve does not exist — is this a Proxmox host?"
38	    exit 1
39	fi
40	
41	# Plain-text state snapshots, gathered into the archive alongside the raw config.
42	# A rebuilder needs to know what the pools/versions/interfaces *were*, and none of
43	# that is recoverable from /etc/pve alone.
44	work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-config-backup.XXXXXX)" || { log "FAIL: mktemp"; exit 1; }
45	trap 'rm -rf "${work}"' EXIT
46	snap="${work}/state"
47	mkdir -p "${snap}"
48	
49	{
50	    echo "# Nxeon host state snapshot — ${TS}"
51	    echo "# hostname: $(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
52	} > "${snap}/README.txt"
53	
54	pveversion -v            >"${snap}/pveversion.txt"      2>&1 || true
55	pvesm status             >"${snap}/pvesm-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
56	qm list                  >"${snap}/qm-list.txt"         2>&1 || true
57	zpool status             >"${snap}/zpool-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
58	zfs list -o name,used,avail,mountpoint >"${snap}/zfs-list.txt" 2>&1 || true
59	ip -o addr               >"${snap}/ip-addr.txt"         2>&1 || true
60	ip route                 >"${snap}/ip-route.txt"        2>&1 || true
61	iptables-save            >"${snap}/iptables-save.txt"   2>&1 || true
62	systemctl list-unit-files 'nxeon*' --no-legend >"${snap}/nxeon-units.txt" 2>&1 || true
63	lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT >"${snap}/lsblk.txt" 2>&1 || true
64	
65	# What goes in. Every path here is either irreplaceable (VM definitions, cluster
66	# keys, TLS material, the panel's own env) or expensive to reconstruct by hand.
67	PATHS=(
68	    /etc/pve                        # VM/CT definitions, storage.cfg, user.cfg, firewall, priv/
69	    /etc/nxeon                      # panel env: offsite target, Cloudflare, mail, TLS
70	    /etc/network/interfaces         # bridges the guests are attached to
71	    /etc/hostname
72	    /etc/hosts
73	    /etc/fstab
74	    /etc/resolv.conf
75	)
76	# Optional extras — included only if present, never a reason to fail.
77	for p in /etc/nginx /etc/postfix /etc/apt/sources.list /etc/apt/sources.list.d /var/spool/cron/crontabs; do
78	    [ -e "$p" ] && PATHS+=("$p")
79	done
80	# The Nxeon systemd units themselves (service/timer/drop-in), collected by glob.
81	mapfile -t NXEON_UNITS < <(find /etc/systemd/system -maxdepth 2 -name 'nxeon-*' 2>/dev/null)
82	
83	tmp="${DEST}.partial"
84	# 0600 from the moment it exists: this archive contains /etc/pve/priv (cluster and
85	# CA keys) and /etc/nxeon (API tokens, mail credentials). It must never be
86	# world-readable on a 0755 directory.
87	( umask 077
88	  tar -czf "${tmp}" \
89	      --warning=no-file-changed --warning=no-file-ignored \
90	      -C "${work}" state \
91	      "${PATHS[@]}" "${NXEON_UNITS[@]}" 2>"${work}/tar.err" )
92	rc=$?
93	
94	# tar exit 1 == "some files changed while reading" (normal for the pmxcfs FUSE
95	# mount and for live logs). Only exit >= 2 is a real failure.
96	if [ "${rc}" -ge 2 ] || [ ! -s "${tmp}" ]; then
97	    log "FAIL: tar exited ${rc}"
98	    sed -n '1,20p' "${work}/tar.err" 2>/dev/null | while read -r l; do log "  tar: ${l}"; done
99	    rm -f "${tmp}"
100	    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"tar exited %s"}\n' "$(date -Is)" "${rc}" \
101	        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
102	    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
103	    exit 1
104	fi
105	[ "${rc}" -eq 1 ] && log "note: tar reported files changed during read (expected for /etc/pve)"
106	
107	mv "${tmp}" "${DEST}"
108	chmod 600 "${DEST}"
109	
110	# Integrity check: an archive that cannot be listed is not a backup. Assert the
111	# VM definitions are actually inside it — a silently empty tarball that reports
112	# success is the failure mode this whole file exists to prevent.
113	if ! tar -tzf "${DEST}" >"${work}/list.txt" 2>&1; then
114	    log "FAIL: ${DEST} is not a readable gzip archive"
115	    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"archive unreadable"}\n' "$(date -Is)" \
116	        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
117	    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
118	    exit 1
119	fi
120	# /etc/pve/qemu-server is a symlink into nodes/<node>/qemu-server, and tar stores
121	# the symlink rather than following it — so the real definitions land under the
122	# nodes/ path. Match both spellings; this assertion already caught the narrower
123	# pattern silently "succeeding" with zero VM configs on its first run.
124	confs=$(grep -cE 'etc/pve/(nodes/[^/]+/)?qemu-server/[0-9]+\.conf$' "${work}/list.txt" || true)
125	if [ "${confs}" -lt 1 ]; then
126	    log "FAIL: ${DEST} contains no /etc/pve/qemu-server/*.conf — VM definitions missing"
127	    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"no VM definitions in archive"}\n' "$(date -Is)" \
128	        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
129	    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
130	    exit 1
131	fi
132	
133	size=$(stat -c%s "${DEST}")
134	# Report the apparent size, not `du` — ZFS compression makes `du` report 512 for a
135	# 48 KB archive, which reads like a truncated/empty backup at a glance.
136	log "OK ${DEST} (${size} bytes, ${confs} VM definition(s))"
137	
138	# Retention: keep the newest KEEP_LAST host-config archives. Scoped by an exact
139	# filename pattern in one directory, so it can only ever match archives this
140	# script wrote — never a vzdump archive, never a customer's anything.
141	mapfile -t old < <(ls -1t "${DEST_DIR}"/host-config-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | tail -n "+$((KEEP_LAST + 1))")
142	for f in "${old[@]:-}"; do
143	    [ -n "${f}" ] || continue
144	    log "pruning ${f} (keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"
145	    rm -f -- "${f}"
146	done
147	
148	printf '{"ok":true,"at":"%s","archive":"%s","bytes":%s,"vmDefinitions":%s,"keepLast":%s}\n' \
149	    "$(date -Is)" "${DEST}" "${size}" "${confs}" "${KEEP_LAST}" \
150	    > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
151	chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
152	
153	log "done"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ============================================================================
3	# guest-backup-coverage.sh — is each guest ACTUALLY covered by a platform backup?
4	# ============================================================================
5	# Prints one line per guest, `<vmid> <verdict> <detail>`, and exits 0. Verdicts:
6	#
7	#   OK       a fresh archive exists that belongs to THIS guest
8	#   MISSING  no archive at all for this vmid
9	#   STALE    newest archive is older than the freshness bound
10	#   FOREIGN  newest archive PREDATES the guest's creation, so it is a previous
11	#            tenant's archive sitting under a recycled vmid
12	#
13	# WHY THIS IS NOT `ls vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-*`
14	# -----------------------------------------
15	# Filename existence answers "has this NUMBER ever been backed up", which is a
16	# different question from "is this GUEST protected", and the two come apart in
17	# two ways that both report healthy:
18	#
19	#   STALE   — a guest whose backup has failed every night for a month still has
20	#             its first archive on disk, so a glob matches. An aggregate "newest
21	#             archive on the platform" check cannot see it either: one healthy
22	#             guest keeps the fleet number green while any number of individual
23	#             guests rot.
24	#
25	#   FOREIGN — Proxmox `/cluster/nextid` hands out the LOWEST free vmid, so a
26	#             destroyed guest's number is recycled to the next customer, while
27	#             archives named after that number persist (vzdump retention is
28	#             keep-last per vmid and knows nothing about whose vmid it was). A
29	#             brand-new customer therefore inherits a full set of "coverage" from
30	#             the tenant before them and reports protected having never been
31	#             backed up. The same archives are the previous tenant's data sitting
32	#             under the new tenant's number.
33	#
34	# The anchor for FOREIGN is Proxmox's own record of when the guest was created:
35	# the `meta:` line in /etc/pve/qemu-server/<vmid>.conf carries `ctime=<epoch>`,
36	# written once at create time and untouched by later edits — so it survives the
37	# rename/reconfigure churn that makes file mtimes useless here. When that line is
38	# absent (guests predating PVE writing it) the check degrades to freshness only,
39	# which is the safe direction: it never invents a creation date.
40	#
41	# Read-only. Touches no VM, deletes nothing.
42	#
43	# Overrides (all default to the live host; the test suite uses them for fixtures):
44	#   NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR   archive directory      (/tank/backup/platform)
45	#   NXEON_PVE_CONF_DIR          guest configs          (/etc/pve/qemu-server)
46	#   NXEON_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS  freshness bound        (48)
47	#   NXEON_COVERAGE_VMIDS        whitespace-separated vmid list, bypassing `qm list`
48	#   NXEON_COVERAGE_NOW          epoch seconds to treat as "now"
49	set -uo pipefail
50	
51	PLATFORM_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
52	CONF_DIR="${NXEON_PVE_CONF_DIR:-/etc/pve/qemu-server}"
53	MAX_AGE_H="${NXEON_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS:-48}"
54	NOW="${NXEON_COVERAGE_NOW:-$(date +%s)}"
55	
56	# Guest list: customer + platform guests, 100 <= vmid < 9000. Templates (9000+)
57	# are excluded — they are reproducible from scripts/build-templates.sh and are not
58	# anybody's data.
59	if [ -n "${NXEON_COVERAGE_VMIDS:-}" ]; then
60	    VMID_SRC="${NXEON_COVERAGE_VMIDS}"
61	else
62	    VMID_SRC="$(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}')"
63	fi
64	
65	for vmid in ${VMID_SRC}; do
66	    [ -n "${vmid}" ] || continue
67	
68	    newest="$(ls -1t "${PLATFORM_DIR}/vzdump-qemu-${vmid}-"*.vma* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
69	    if [ -z "${newest}" ]; then
70	        printf '%s MISSING no archive for this vmid\n' "${vmid}"
71	        continue
72	    fi
73	
74	    arch_ts="$(stat -c %Y "${newest}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
75	    age_h=$(( ( NOW - arch_ts ) / 3600 ))
76	    base="$(basename "${newest}")"
77	
78	    created="$(sed -n 's/^meta:.*ctime=\([0-9]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p' \
79	        "${CONF_DIR}/${vmid}.conf" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
80	    [ -n "${created}" ] || created=0
81	
82	    # FOREIGN outranks STALE: "this is somebody else's archive" is a different and
83	    # worse fact than "this guest's archive is old", and reporting it as merely
84	    # stale would suggest the next nightly run fixes it.
85	    if [ "${created}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${arch_ts}" -lt "${created}" ]; then
86	        printf '%s FOREIGN %s predates guest creation (archive %s < created %s) — previous tenant of this vmid\n' \
87	            "${vmid}" "${base}" "${arch_ts}" "${created}"
88	    elif [ "${age_h}" -ge "${MAX_AGE_H}" ]; then
89	        printf '%s STALE %s is %sh old (>=%sh)\n' "${vmid}" "${base}" "${age_h}" "${MAX_AGE_H}"
90	    else
91	        printf '%s OK %s is %sh old\n' "${vmid}" "${base}" "${age_h}"
92	    fi
93	done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Restore-verification: proves the newest backups are actually restorable.
3	#
4	#   Part 1 (destructive-proof): restores the latest /tank/backup/db/nxeon-*.sql.gz
5	#           into a scratch database and asserts core tables came back with rows.
6	#   Part 2 (structural): asserts the whole-system side exists and is fresh — a
7	#           host-config archive that lists real VM definitions, and a recent VM
8	#           archive per guest. Part 2 is why this script no longer only proves the
9	#           database is safe: on 2026-07-26 the DB half had been green for days
10	#           while the whole-VM half had literally never produced a single archive,
11	#           and this script could not have told anyone.
12	#
13	# Production data is never touched. Exits non-zero on any failure so the systemd
14	# OnFailure hook alerts admins. Also writes a status file for /admin/backups —
15	# without it the panel can only report "the unit exited 0", which is precisely the
16	# signal that proved worthless for the off-site job.
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
20	PLATFORM_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
21	STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
22	STATUS="${STATUS_DIR}/verify-restore.json"
23	SCRATCH="nxeon_restore_verify"
24	LOG="/tmp/nxeon-verify-restore.log"
25	MAX_AGE_H="${NXEON_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS:-48}"
26	
27	log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }
28	
29	mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true
30	
31	WARNINGS=""
32	warn() { log "WARNING: $*"; WARNINGS="${WARNINGS}${WARNINGS:+; }$*"; }
33	
34	write_status() {
35	    printf '{"ok":%s,"at":"%s","dbDump":"%s","dbAgeHours":%s,"vmArchives":%s,"vmNewestAgeHours":%s,"hostConfigVmDefs":%s,"warnings":"%s","error":%s}\n' \
36	        "$1" "$(date -Is)" "${DB_DUMP_NAME:-}" "${DB_AGE_H:--1}" "${VM_ARCHIVES:--1}" \
37	        "${VM_AGE_H:--1}" "${CONF_DEFS:--1}" "${WARNINGS}" "$2" > "${STATUS}"
38	    chmod 644 "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null || true
39	}
40	
41	fail() {
42	    log "FAIL: $*"
43	    sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
44	    write_status false "\"$*\""
45	    exit 1
46	}
47	
48	DB_DUMP_NAME=""; DB_AGE_H=-1; VM_ARCHIVES=-1; VM_AGE_H=-1; CONF_DEFS=-1
49	
50	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Part 1 — the database dump really restores
52	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	LATEST="$(ls -1t "${BACKUP_DIR}"/nxeon-*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
54	[ -n "${LATEST}" ] || fail "no production dump found in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
55	DB_DUMP_NAME="$(basename "${LATEST}")"
56	
57	DB_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${LATEST}") ) / 3600 ))
58	log "verifying ${LATEST} (age ${DB_AGE_H}h, $(stat -c%s "${LATEST}") bytes)"
59	[ "${DB_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest DB dump is ${DB_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h)"
60	
61	# gzip integrity first — a corrupt archive should fail loudly.
62	gzip -t "${LATEST}" || fail "gzip integrity check failed"
63	
64	sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
65	sudo -u postgres psql -qc "CREATE DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null || fail "could not create scratch db"
66	
67	if ! zcat "${LATEST}" | sudo -u postgres psql -q "${SCRATCH}" >"${LOG}" 2>&1; then
68	  log "psql restore returned non-zero; see ${LOG}"
69	fi
70	ERRS=$(grep -ci '^ERROR' "${LOG}" || true)
71	[ "${ERRS}" -eq 0 ] || { log "restore produced ${ERRS} errors:"; grep -i '^ERROR' "${LOG}" | head -5; fail "restore had errors"; }
72	
73	# Core tables must exist and hold rows — an empty "successful" restore is a failure.
74	for t in User OsTemplate Plan Server; do
75	  n=$(sudo -u postgres psql -tA "${SCRATCH}" -c "select count(*) from \"${t}\";" 2>/dev/null || echo "x")
76	  [[ "${n}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "table ${t} missing from restored dump"
77	  [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] || fail "table ${t} restored with 0 rows"
78	  log "OK ${t}=${n}"
79	done
80	
81	sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null
82	log "DB restore verification PASSED (scratch db dropped, production untouched)"
83	
84	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	# Part 2 — the whole-system side exists and is fresh
86	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	# Not a real restore: qmrestore of a 10 GB guest onto a live host is not something
88	# a weekly timer should do unsupervised. What it DOES assert is everything that was
89	# false on this box for its first four days of life — that host-level archives
90	# exist at all, that they are recent, that one exists per running guest, and that
91	# the host-config tarball actually contains VM definitions rather than being an
92	# empty tarball that reported success.
93	CONF="$(ls -1t "${PLATFORM_DIR}"/host-config-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
94	if [ -z "${CONF}" ]; then
95	    fail "no host-config-*.tar.gz in ${PLATFORM_DIR} — /etc/pve is not backed up, a bare-metal rebuild would have no VM definitions"
96	fi
97	CONF_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${CONF}") ) / 3600 ))
98	CONF_DEFS=$(tar -tzf "${CONF}" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE 'etc/pve/(nodes/[^/]+/)?qemu-server/[0-9]+\.conf$' || true)
99	[ "${CONF_DEFS}" -gt 0 ] || fail "$(basename "${CONF}") contains no VM definitions"
100	log "OK host config $(basename "${CONF}") (age ${CONF_AGE_H}h, ${CONF_DEFS} VM definition(s))"
101	[ "${CONF_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest host-config archive is ${CONF_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h)"
102	
103	VM_ARCHIVES=$(find "${PLATFORM_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'vzdump-*.vma*' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
104	if [ "${VM_ARCHIVES}" -eq 0 ]; then
105	    fail "no whole-system VM archives in ${PLATFORM_DIR} — the nxeon-backup-vms timer has produced nothing"
106	fi
107	NEWEST_VM="$(ls -1t "${PLATFORM_DIR}"/vzdump-*.vma* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
108	VM_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${NEWEST_VM}") ) / 3600 ))
109	log "OK ${VM_ARCHIVES} VM archive(s) present, newest $(basename "${NEWEST_VM}") (age ${VM_AGE_H}h)"
110	[ "${VM_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest VM archive is ${VM_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h) — the daily backup is not running"
111	
112	# Per-guest coverage: a running guest with no archive is invisible in an aggregate
113	# count. This is how "the platform has 40 archives" can still mean "vmid 104 has
114	# never been backed up".
115	#
116	# EXISTENCE IS NOT COVERAGE. This check used to be a bare `compgen -G` for
117	# `vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-*`, which asks only "does a file with this vmid in its name
118	# exist". Two ways that answers yes while the guest is in fact unprotected:
119	#
120	#   1. STALE. A guest whose backups have failed every night for a month still has
121	#      its day-one archive sitting in the directory, so the glob matches and the
122	#      guest reports covered. The aggregate freshness check above cannot catch
123	#      this either: it only looks at the newest archive on the whole platform, so
124	#      one healthy guest's nightly archive keeps the fleet number green while any
125	#      number of individual guests rot.
126	#
127	#   2. INHERITED FROM THE PREVIOUS TENANT. Proxmox's /cluster/nextid hands out the
128	#      LOWEST free vmid, so a destroyed guest's number is recycled to the next
129	#      customer provisioned — while the archives named after that number persist,
130	#      because vzdump retention is keep-last per vmid and knows nothing about
131	#      whose vmid it was. A brand-new customer on a recycled vmid therefore
132	#      inherits a full set of "coverage" from the tenant before them, and reports
133	#      protected from the moment it is created, having never been backed up.
134	#      (It is also the reverse of the disclosure hazard: those archives are the
135	#      old tenant's data still sitting under the new tenant's number.)
136	#
137	# So coverage is asserted against the guest, not the filename: the newest archive
138	# must be FRESH, and it must POSTDATE THE GUEST'S OWN CREATION. Proxmox records
139	# creation epoch in the config's `meta:` line (`ctime=`), which is written once at
140	# create time and is not touched by later edits — so it survives exactly the
141	# rename/reconfigure churn that makes file mtimes useless here. A guest whose
142	# newest archive predates its own creation is being covered by somebody else's
143	# backup, which is not coverage at all.
144	# The verdicts come from scripts/guest-backup-coverage.sh so the same rules can be
145	# unit-tested against fixtures (test/guest-backup-coverage.test.ts) instead of only
146	# ever running here, against the one live directory, once a day.
147	COVERAGE_SCRIPT="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/guest-backup-coverage.sh"
148	if [ ! -x "${COVERAGE_SCRIPT}" ]; then
149	    warn "per-guest coverage NOT checked: ${COVERAGE_SCRIPT} missing or not executable"
150	else
151	    while read -r vmid verdict detail; do
152	        [ -n "${vmid}" ] || continue
153	        case "${verdict}" in
154	            OK)      log "OK guest ${vmid} covered (${detail})" ;;
155	            MISSING) warn "guest ${vmid} has NO whole-system archive" ;;
156	            STALE)   warn "guest ${vmid}: ${detail}" ;;
157	            FOREIGN) warn "guest ${vmid}: ${detail}" ;;
158	            *)       warn "guest ${vmid}: unrecognised coverage verdict '${verdict}' ${detail}" ;;
159	        esac
160	    done < <(NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR="${PLATFORM_DIR}" \
161	             NXEON_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS="${MAX_AGE_H}" \
162	             "${COVERAGE_SCRIPT}" 2>/dev/null)
163	fi
164	
165	if [ -n "${WARNINGS}" ]; then
166	    log "restore verification PASSED WITH WARNINGS: ${WARNINGS}"
167	else
168	    log "restore verification PASSED (database restorable; whole-system archives present and fresh)"
169	fi
170	write_status true null

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
4	# =============================================================================
5	# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
6	# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
7	# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
8	# current state before changing anything.
9	#
10	# What it does:
11	#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
12	#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
13	#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
14	#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
15	#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
16	#      needs (documented pveum commands)
17	#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
18	#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
19	#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
20	#
21	# SAFETY:
22	#   - Never flushes the firewall. It only APPENDS its own MASQUERADE/FORWARD
23	#     rules and only if an identical rule is not already present.
24	#   - Never touches running VMs. Template builds skip any VMID that exists.
25	#   - Never destroys storage. `pvesm add` is skipped when the storage id exists.
26	#
27	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	# CROSS-HOST NETWORKING — IMPORTANT LIMITATION (read before deploying node #2)
29	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	# Each node NATs its OWN private /24 (10.20.N.0/24) behind its OWN public IP.
31	# This makes each node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation and
32	# SSH DNAT — but it does NOT give VMs on different physical hosts a shared LAN.
33	#
34	#   * A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the
35	#     private network. They are separate NAT islands.
36	#   * The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the
37	#     DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on.
38	#
39	# If you need private east-west connectivity between VMs on different nodes you
40	# must lay an overlay/VPN over the public IPs — e.g. WireGuard mesh or a VXLAN
41	# fabric (Proxmox SDN "VXLAN zone") — and route the /24s across it. That is out
42	# of scope for this script; it is a deliberate, documented follow-up. For the
43	# common case (independent single-node VPS customers) per-node NAT islands are
44	# exactly what you want.
45	#
46	# Assumption: node #2 is a SEPARATE physical box with its own public IP, NOT a
47	# second NIC on the same L2 as node #1. If two nodes truly share L2 you would
48	# instead give them the SAME bridge/subnet and split the IP range — but this
49	# script assumes the separate-host model above.
50	# =============================================================================
51	set -euo pipefail
52	
53	# ---------- Parameters (flags override env) ----------------------------------
54	NODE_NUM="${NODE_NUM:-2}"           # ordinal; drives subnet + nat chain defaults
55	SUBNET_OCTET=""                     # third octet of 10.20.X.0/24 (default: NODE_NUM-1)
56	PUBLIC_IP="${PUBLIC_IP:-}"          # this host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if empty)
57	BRIDGE=""                           # vmbrX (default: vmbr1)
58	NVME_STORAGE="${NVME_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
59	HDD_STORAGE="${HDD_STORAGE:-vmdata-hdd}"
60	NVME_ZPOOL="${NVME_ZPOOL:-}"        # existing ZFS pool for NVMe storage (optional)
61	HDD_DIR="${HDD_DIR:-/tank/backup}"  # dir-backed HDD storage path
62	SNIPPETS_STORAGE="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE:-$HDD_STORAGE}"
63	TOKEN_USER="${TOKEN_USER:-nxeon@pve}"
64	TOKEN_NAME="${TOKEN_NAME:-platform}"
65	TOKEN_ROLE="${TOKEN_ROLE:-NxeonProvision}"
66	BUILD_TEMPLATES="${BUILD_TEMPLATES:-0}"   # 1 = build 9000-9004 here; 0 = document copying
67	SSH_PORT_START="${SSH_PORT_START:-20000}"
68	SSH_PORT_END="${SSH_PORT_END:-29999}"
69	
70	usage() {
71	  cat <<EOF
72	Usage: $0 [flags]
73	  --node-num N          Node ordinal (default 2). Sets defaults for subnet + nat chain.
74	  --subnet-octet N      Third octet of the /24 (default: node-num - 1, e.g. node 2 -> 1 -> 10.20.1.0/24).
75	  --public-ip IP        This host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if omitted).
76	  --bridge vmbrX        NAT bridge name (default vmbr1).
77	  --nvme-storage NAME   NVMe storage id (default vmdata).
78	  --hdd-storage NAME    HDD storage id (default vmdata-hdd).
79	  --nvme-zpool POOL     Existing ZFS pool to back the NVMe storage (zfspool). Optional.
80	  --hdd-dir PATH        Directory for the HDD (dir) storage (default /tank/backup).
81	  --build-templates     Build cloud-init templates 9000-9004 on this host.
82	  -h, --help            Show this help.
83	
84	Environment variables mirror the flags (NODE_NUM, PUBLIC_IP, BRIDGE, ...).
85	EOF
86	}
87	
88	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
89	  case "$1" in
90	    --node-num) NODE_NUM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
91	    --subnet-octet) SUBNET_OCTET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
92	    --public-ip) PUBLIC_IP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
93	    --bridge) BRIDGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
94	    --nvme-storage) NVME_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
95	    --hdd-storage) HDD_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
96	    --nvme-zpool) NVME_ZPOOL="$2"; shift 2 ;;

248	# Role privileges: everything the worker/web need to clone, configure, run and
249	# monitor VMs, allocate cloud-init, and read node/storage status. Mirrors the

251	#
252	# VM.GuestAgent.Audit is REQUIRED for in-guest disk sampling: the monitor calls

261	# NB: do NOT add VM.Monitor here — it was removed in Proxmox VE 9 and `pveum role
262	# modify` rejects the whole call with "invalid privilege 'VM.Monitor'" (400),

276	else

279	fi

282	if pveum user list 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "$TOKEN_USER"; then
283	  ok "user ${TOKEN_USER} exists"
284	else
285	  pveum user add "$TOKEN_USER"
286	  ok "created user ${TOKEN_USER}"
287	fi
288	
289	# Grant the role at / (propagating). Idempotent — re-running is harmless.
290	pveum acl modify / --users "$TOKEN_USER" --roles "$TOKEN_ROLE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
291	ok "granted ${TOKEN_ROLE} to ${TOKEN_USER} at / (propagate)"
292	
293	# Token. If it already exists we cannot re-read the secret (Proxmox only shows it
294	# once at creation), so we leave it and tell the operator to reuse the stored one
295	# or delete+recreate.

302	else

304	  TOKEN_OUT="$(pveum user token add "$TOKEN_USER" "$TOKEN_NAME" --privsep 0 2>/dev/null || true)"

311	  fi
312	fi

333	  fi
334	else

336	  cat <<EOF

338	  copy them from the primary node so every node clones byte-identical images:
339

342	    # Copy the resulting vzdump-qemu-90XX*.vma.* files to this host, then:

347	    done
348	
349	  Or run:  BUILD_TEMPLATES=1 $0 --node-num ${NODE_NUM}   to build them locally.
350	EOF
351	fi
352	
353	# =============================================================================
354	# 7. Print the Add-node form values
355	# =============================================================================
356	log "[7/7] Done. Paste these into Nxeon → Admin → Compute nodes → Add node:"
357	API_URL="https://${PUBLIC_IP}:8006"
358	cat <<EOF
359	
360	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
361	  │  Nxeon "Add node" form values                                           │
362	  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
363	  Node name        : node-${NODE_NUM}
364	  pveNode          : ${PVE_NODE}
365	  API URL          : ${API_URL}
366	  Public IP        : ${PUBLIC_IP}
367	  Token ID         : ${TOKEN_USER}!${TOKEN_NAME}
368	  Token secret     : ${TOKEN_SECRET:-<shown once at token creation — reuse your saved value>}

content.thinking:
These systemd services and timers are all documented as running on the control-plane host, the primary node, with no indication they're deployed per-node or exist on node-2. The onboard-node.sh script explicitly doesn't install them there.

Confirming onboard-node.sh only sets up Proxmox-specific resources (bridge, storage, token, templates) for API connectivity, not firewall or backup infrastructure. ---

# P2 — error paths and hardening

1. **No irreversible destroy is confirmed server-side.** Every destroy relies on a browser
   `window.confirm`; the action takes a bare id — `lib/actions.ts:445-485` (`delete`/`reinstall`),
   `lib/actions-volumes.ts:167` (`deleteVolume`), `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:81`
   (`reinstallToOs` — the "type ERASE" gate is client-only at `components/customer/ReinstallOs.tsx:39`),
   `lib/actions-server.ts:66` (`rollbackSnapshot` — no status check, no confirmation),
   `lib/actions-databases.ts:168`, `lib/actions-websites.ts:295`. Next.js validates the Origin header
   on server actions so this is not remotely exploitable; the impact is accidental/scripted invocation
   with no server-side "are you sure", no soft-delete, no undo. Note the **admin** delete requires
   typing the hostname (`components/admin/ServerAdminActions.tsx:52`) — the customer's own irreversible
   purge is easier to fire than the admin's. `deleteMyAccount` (`lib/actions-gdpr.ts:65`) gets it right.
2. **Control-panel delete paths skip the lifecycle-busy guard.** Create paths check `lifecycleBusy` +
   `status === "RUNNING"` (`actions-databases.ts:123-125`, `actions-websites.ts:215-217`,
   `actions-apps.ts:142-144`); the delete paths (`actions-databases.ts:168-183`,
   `actions-websites.ts:295-312`, `actions-apps.ts:229-261`) check neither. A `DB_DELETE` can be queued
   during a `BACKUP_RESTORE`/`RESIZE`/`DISK_EXPAND`, racing SSH work against a resizing root filesystem.
3. **`deleteVolume` is less defended than the non-destructive expand path** — `lib/actions-volumes.ts:167`
   has no `DETACHED` requirement (an actively-written volume can be destroyed), no rate limit and no
   `assertNotImpersonating()`, whereas `lib/actions-disk.ts:42, 52-61` has both on the *growth* path.
4. **One job at a time, platform-wide.** `worker/index.ts:1142` — a `MIGRATE` or a `BACKUP_RESTORE`
   (`worker/restore.ts:125`, `timeoutMs: 3_600_000`) blocks every other customer's provisioning,
   deletion and backup for its full duration; a timed-out restore retries twice more (`MAX_ATTEMPTS =
   3`) for up to 3 hours of queue stall. No retry backoff either — a failed job returns straight to
   `QUEUED` (`:962`) and is re-claimed on the next 3s poll.
5. **Check-then-act on the one-in-flight-job rule.** `applyResize` (`lib/resize.ts:100-131`),
   `applyDiskExpand` (`lib/disk-expand.ts:155-202`) and `queueJob` (`lib/actions-server.ts:31-36`) count
   pending jobs *outside* the transaction that debits and enqueues. Two concurrent requests (two tabs,
   or a retry after a proxy timeout) both see zero and both charge. `orderVolume`
   (`lib/actions-volumes.ts:55-110`) has no guard at all. The codebase already has the right tool —
   `beginSubmit()` (`lib/actions-domains.ts:42-53`) — but it is private to the domains file.
6. **The public status page crashes instead of reporting a DB outage.** `lib/monitoring.ts:324` does
   `Promise.all([dbHealth(), workerHealth(), proxmoxHealth()])`; `workerHealth()` has no try/catch, so a
   DB outage rejects the whole report and `app/status/page.tsx` renders the error boundary. The one
   component `/status` exists to report on is the one it cannot report. (`/api/health` handles this
   correctly at `route.ts:64-67`.)
7. **Calendar mutations pass an attacker-controlled URL to the DAV client with credentials attached.**
   `lib/actions-calendar.ts:215-236` (`updateEvent`), `:239-245` (`deleteEvent`), `:289-304`, `:307-313`
   take an `id` that is a raw object href and hand it to `putObjectAt`/`deleteObjectAt`
   (`lib/calendar/caldav.ts:180, :194`), which PUT/DELETE that exact URL with the caller's Basic-auth
   header. `assertOwnedCalendar` (`:107`) exists and is used by `createEvent`/`createTask` but not by
   the four mutate-by-href paths, and nothing checks the href is under `CALDAV_BASE`. Blind SSRF from
   inside the network, with the caller's mailbox credentials in the `Authorization` header.
8. **Impersonated actions are audit-logged as the customer everywhere except `lib/actions.ts`.**
   `lib/actions.ts:51-58` is the only `audit()` helper that stamps `actingAdmin=<id>`. Every other
   action file writes `userId: user.id` with no marker — `lib/actions-server-extra.ts:35`,
   `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:595, :717`, `lib/actions-websites.ts`, `lib/actions-databases.ts`,
   `lib/actions-cron.ts`. An admin acting under impersonation is indistinguishable from the customer.
9. **`bulkVoidInvoices` voids REFUNDED invoices; the single-invoice action refuses.**
   `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:189` includes `REFUNDED` in `voidable` and clears `paidAt`; its own
   docstring one line above says nothing about it, and `voidInvoice` (`lib/actions-billing.ts:54-67`)
   refuses anything PAID. A refunded invoice silently becomes VOID and drops out of the "Issued · total"
   stat (`app/admin/invoices/page.tsx:31`) — the refund trail is erased from the invoice ledger.
10. **Guard mismatch on the invoice detail page.** `app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:23` gates on
    `requireArea("billing")` but the actions it exposes gate on `requireAdmin()`
    (`lib/actions-billing.ts:55, 71`), which `redirect()`s. `components/admin/InvoiceAdmin.tsx:17-27`
    catches and displays `e.message`, so a BILLING-role staffer clicking **Mark paid** sees an opaque
    `NEXT_REDIRECT` string in a red error span instead of a permission message.
11. **Coupon toggle/delete have no error surface.** `components/admin/CouponControls.tsx:85, :100` call
    `Promise<void>` actions inside `startTransition` with no try/catch and no `router.refresh()`. A DB
    failure replaces the whole page with the `app/admin/error.tsx` boundary.
12. **Node edit form: "leave blank to keep unchanged" is impossible.**
    `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx:115-121` renders the API token with
    `placeholder="•••••• stored — leave blank to keep unchanged"` and `defaultValue=""`, but `Field`
    defaults to `required = true` (`:63`) and `lib/actions-nodes.ts:59` is `z.string().min(1)` with no
    blank-means-keep branch. The admin must re-paste the full Proxmox token to change *anything* on a node.
13. **`/admin/abuse` points admins at Settings fields that don't exist.**
    `app/admin/abuse/page.tsx:30-32` says thresholds `abuse_outbound_mbps` / `abuse_autosuspend` are
    "in Settings". Both keys are real and read by `worker/abuse.ts:19-20`, but neither appears in
    `SECTION_FIELDS.security` (`lib/actions-settings.ts:83-88`) nor in `SecurityPanel.tsx`. The only way
    to change them is a manual DB write.

**Also worth fixing, lower confidence / latent:**

* **No VMID 9000–9999 guard on any destructive path.** The only `9000` comparison in the codebase is a
  display filter (`app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx:244`). `destroyVm` (`worker/index.ts:357`), both resize
  PUTs (`:308, :581`, `worker/disk-expand.ts:344`) and the volume config mutators take `vmid` straight
  from the DB. Not reachable today — `Server.vmid` is only written by `provision()` from
  `/cluster/nextid` — but one bad DB fix-up from destroying the Ubuntu template. Add `assertCustomerVmid()`.
* **`nodeId` nullable with a primary-node fallback** (`worker/index.ts:69-78`, `worker/volumes.ts:37-61`,
  `worker/disk-expand.ts:82-97`) and **`listBackups` ignoring the server's node** (`lib/proxmox.ts:397`).
